entities.name: John Fane, 11th Earl of Westmorland
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
John Fane, 11th Earl of Westmorland, styled Lord Burghersh until 1841, was a British soldier, politician, diplomat, composer and musician.

Born into the powerful Fane family, John Fane was educated at Eton College and later studied at Christ Church, Oxford. He entered the British Army at 18 and saw action in the Indian Rebellion of 1857, where he was appointed commander of the 1st Westmorland regiment.

A member of the Conservative Party, Fane served as a Member of Parliament for the constituency of Westmorland from 1841 to 1859. He also held diplomatic posts in India and the Middle East, where he played a key role in securing British interests during the Crimean War.

In addition to his military and political pursuits, Fane was a talented composer and musician. He wrote several works, including a set of cantatas for the church choir at his family's estate in Westmorland.

Fane's legacy extends beyond his personal achievements. His family's influence in Westmorland continued through his son, the 12th Earl of Westmorland, who played a significant role in the development of the local economy and politics.

The Fane family's Westmorland estate, once a major center of power and influence, remains a testament to their enduring legacy in the region.

John Fane's life serves as a reminder of the complex interplay between politics, diplomacy, and cultural expression in the 19th century.
